So, therefore, the challenge to the reliability seems to be at different levels, if I understood you well, Mr. Tieger, and if I understood your reference well, Mr. Misetic. We'll move --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may quickly respond. I will be very quick. First of all, just two quick points. With respect to motivation for any systematic collection of documentation related to shelling, there's been -- there's considerable evidence that has been cited before and -- about concern by Croatian authorities with regard to indictments. That's number one. Number two -- I said they would be quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, very quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the second one is with respect to the systematic collection, the Court has received new information in the November 30th submission by Croatian authorities in the accompanying order that indicates that documents related to Storm were -- there was an effort to collect them systematically outside the normal archiving process. And that's the reference -- or at least one of the references to which I referred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please be very precise. You are drawing our attention to apparently a portion of the material that was submitted. Could you give us more details as you find it there in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just as a procedural matter, now Mr. Tieger has said that the report of November 30th has submitted to the Chamber; that's something that is news to us, and we have no such report. We have a report from the 14th of December and the 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm referring to tab 6 of the filing we made on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then it's clear that is the communication between the Office of the Prosecutor and the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But what I'm referring to is documentation submitted in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll have a -- Now, Mr. Misetic, it is clear what we are talking about, at least, and the Chamber will then ... I'd like to move on to my next series, which is number 94. 94 is not a series, but can be placed in the context of 95. 94 and 95 have similarity with 74 and 75 and 84 and 85. It is reporting from TS-4 to the Operational Group Sibenik. Now, for the 5th of August, a morning and afternoon report were received. The same is true for the 4th of August, the day prior. But for the 6th of August, only one report has been produced. Now, first of all, there seems to be some disagreement on whether 94 or 95 is missing. It seems that 95 has been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think it's the other way around, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At least as I understand it, yes. And if I can short circuit this discussion perhaps. If I understand the position of the -- essentially, let me say this. There is -- there has been information provided to us about the relocation of TS-4 on the 6th, and in light of that circumstance, the fact that the relocation on that date was confirmed and the unbroken reference numbers, we accept that number 95 would not have been produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, relocation at what time on that day? Is there ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Or at least that there's a sufficiently credible argument for this not to be a disputed document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any further information as to the time of the relocation of TS-4 on the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No specific time, Your Honour, but in the afternoon, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, there's no dispute anymore about the non-existence and therefore non-production of the second report of the 6th of August by TS-4 to Operational Group Sibenik. Then that matter has been resolved. We need another break. It takes an enormous amount of time to go through all this in quite some detail and to hear the explanations and to see where the real differences are. The Chamber is considering whether there would be any option to have this kind of - if could I say - to some extent, bookkeeping sessions, let's look at the last series. If the Chamber would have known that there's no dispute anymore about the second report of the 6th of August, we would not have had time to prepare for it, neither would there have been a reason to deal with the matter here in court. We had similar matters earlier, which apparently were easily resolved. The Chamber is considering, because we will not finish today, to continue -- I would say the technical aspects of it out of court with representatives of Croatia and the OTP and Defence teams, as they wish, and then to focus in court exclusively on the remaining issues. Because we could spend days and days in court, and the Chamber wants to make it clear to the parties that where artillery documents are an important issue in this case, that it tries to deal with it with highest level of accuracy and precision. The Chamber -- the parties and the Republic of Croatia are invited to think about such solutions or such a way to proceed, which mean everything really contested to be discussed in open court, preparatory meetings, sorting out what really still are the problems, not necessarily to be done in public. The Chamber invites the parties to consider this. We'll now have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move on. I'd like to deal with the following series, which is 134 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I thought it might be helpful if I indicated to the Court certainly consistent with the guidance I think the Court was suggesting earlier, the documents that I believe are not in dispute by -- in addition to the ones we already covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know of many of them you have received, isn't it. But others that are not in dispute, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that would be numbers 134 through 137; 142 through 145; 150 through 153. That is the -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Artillery rocket battalion on the 4th, the 5th and the 6th of August, Mr. Tieger, that's what you're talking about. Because my question was that whether the OTP accepts that they were not were not created or whether they only accepted that the unit was split up, but I do understand now that you accept that they were not created.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in addition, with regard to the same unit, numbers 27 and 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 27 and 29. Thank you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, finally, Your Honour, numbers 156 and 157. As provided, rather than -- rather than not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please. Yes, 156 and 157 were already on my list as being received and therefore not at stake anymore. Then I move on to the following series, which is 98 up to and including 129, which are all regular reports from various operation groups to the -- to Split Military District. Among these, apparently all Operation Group North reports to the Split Military District are missing. Apart from that, 125 is a report, Operation Group Zadar to the Split Military District, is missing as well. So we focus, as a matter of fact, on the missing ones in this series. I took them all together, not to say that they are all missing, but in these reports of operations groups to the Military Districts, all Operation Group North reports are missing and one Operation Group Zadar, which is 125. Let's start with the easy one. In relation to 125, the submissions were not entirely clear, but I think that that was one of the -- you just mentioned, is that -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's some confusion here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 125 is a report -- this is page 55, line 7 -- line 6, I should say. Operation Group -- sorry line 7. 125 is a report, Operation Group Zadar to the Split Military District, and you said is missing as well. And, in fact, it's not missing according to our records. And the OTP has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I wanted to say, that it was at least unclear and that I was inquiring what it exactly was. Let me just check; one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have it as already in the OTP 65 ter exhibit list as 5719.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, it can't be missing. I think it was mainly a matter of unclarity in the submissions than anything else. 125, regular report from OG Zadar to the Split Military District is not in any way missing anymore, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that's correct. And I thought that was encompassed in the -- in one of the earlier submissions. But in any event, one way or another, this is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in dispute. That's most important to establish. Then we don't have to look at any unclarity in any submissions. Then let's focus on the others, which is all the OG North reports to the Split Military District, which is explained by the Republic of Croatia that the Split Military District command and the OG North command were in the same location. We are now returning to an issue similar to the one we discussed before, and that Mr. Ademi was both commander of Operational Group North and Chief of Staff of the Split Military District. The OTP has submitted, in this respect, why this matter was not further explored in the interview with Mr. Ademi, and apart from that, reference is made in this context to the statement of Mr. Rakic, a statement or an Official Note, of an interview of the 17th of January, 2009. Before I give an opportunity to the Prosecution to further explain what reasons they have to assume that these reports do exist, the Chamber wants already to indicate that there are reports mentioned in the submissions by Croatia, I think it was, reports by the Split Military District Command, Zadar forward command post, submitted to OG North, one dated the 4th of August, and there are more examples mentioned there, which seems a bit of a reporting in reversion order. And the Chamber would like to have a look at least some of these documents to better understand how you report from top to bottom, rather than the other way around, because usually orders come from top to bottom, and reports are usually sent from bottom to top. Now, the Chamber, of course, is aware that there was a kind of a personal union and a -- well, to some extent, even perhaps a merger of the organisation, where Mr. Ademi was both Chief of Staff of the Split Military District and the commander of OG North, but it -- the Chamber would like to have a look at that to better understand what the argument is; so, therefore we would like to be provided with at least one or two examples. And then also reports are mentioned, reports by the OG North command, submitted to the Croatian Army Main Staff Operations Command Centre, one dated the 4th of August, one dated the 5th of August, reports apparently signed by Mr. Gotovina. We'd like to have a look at those documents. To be quite honest, I can't say -- they may be already somewhere in evidence, but I'm not at this moment aware of that. We'd like to have a look at those documents primarily in order to understand the submissions by the Republic of Croatia in the context of which we're talking about at this very moment. Mr. Tieger, could you further make further submissions on the matter of the missing reports from OG North to the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the Court appears to be aware of the nature of what I'll call the dispute, although I use that term somewhat guardedly, since it's a matter of an exchange of information here. I don't think I have anything to add to that at this point, except to say that as may have been apparent from the nature of the hearing thus far, there are some documents about which the parties can come to -- some documents in either extreme where one party says it was definitely created, one party says it was definitely not produced. There are various permutations including the documents that remain in dispute, not because the Prosecution necessarily asserts that the position taken by the Republic of Croatia with respect to that particular category of documents is patently untenable, but simply that the information provided thus far is not sufficient in the context of the ongoing investigation to consider the documents no longer at issue, and I just want to make that distinction clear. But apart from that, and I will look at more -- somewhat more -- focus on those particular documents again. But, at the moment, I have nothing to add to the previous submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further submissions to be made by the Republic of Croatia in this context? One of the questions arises, of course, if there is no reporting from an artillery group or artillery rocket group to the operational group, but then, as the next step, also no further reporting up, then it looks as if every information -- even if the two would have merged to some extent, you would expect at least something to remain. And even if one step would be missing in the reporting up, two steps taken in one, then -- but I see that Mr. Misetic wants to most likely say something about what I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we don't agree with that. You would get reporting from the rocket groups to IZM Sajkovici, which is the forward command post of the Split Military District, and that wouldn't necessarily go to OG North. You would also have the reporting in P71 which is diary of the Split Military District, which would record the oral communications coming in via -- via telephone or other electronic equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So it wouldn't necessarily be reporting that would go to OG North and then would go up to the Split Military District --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I suggested that that's not what I intended to say -- I would like to give a opportunity to the representatives of the Republic of Croatia to make further submissions in relation to these reports. Therefore, we're focussing on OG North to the Split Military District, and one of the complaints, it having not been further explored in interviews with Mr. Ademi, and what specific portions of the statement of Mr. Rakic, an interview taken the 17th of January, 2009, where we would have to specifically pay attention to. Yes, Mr. -- will it be you, Mr. Markotic? Or Mr. Crncec? Or Mr. Keser? Well, you're seven, so someone. Yes, Mr. Keser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KESER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, concerning the reports sought that would have been sent from SG-1 to OG Split, we state that the Republic of Croatia believes firmly that these reports needn't to be drafted, not because operation groups in general don't need to report, but because the Operational Group North was specific, as explained already, because of the chain of command. That Operational Group, in Croatia's belief, is synonymous with the main axis of attack. There were no two commands in the same location. There was a single command. A single number of officers working in the same place. There was only one operational centre. For that reason, it would have been illogical to have Operational Group North reporting to the Military District Commander who is in the same location. Furthermore, the documents you referred to put forth by Croatia where the IZM Zadar is reporting to Operational Group North prove that there were differences in the perception of the notion of Operational Group North. This was not a situation in which there would be a reverse process of reporting. In that situation, IZM Zadar is reporting to their superior commander in Sajkovici. IZM Zadar is reporting to the Military District. However, because the title of OG North and the perception of that name as such, that was the name to be included on the list for distribution. The situation with documents remains unclear. Croatia did conduct an interview with General Rahim Ademi. It was established that, at the same time, he was commander of OG North and the Chief of Staff of the Military District. The Official Note, in the latest report which arrived yesterday, is something that we can find, in particular, the last paragraph of his statement, where he directly addresses the issue of reports. I quote: "Concerning regular reports from OG North to ZP or Military District Split, he states that such reports were not drafted because of the aforementioned reason, by which he explained that the commands of OG North and Military District of Split were one and the same." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Tieger, I take it that since one of the submissions by the OTP was that the matter should have been further explored with Mr. Ademi that, apparently, now, in the material that was received yesterday, we may find some further clarification of that. How does the Chamber get hold of at least examples of the documents we refer to; that is, the reports by the Split Military District Commands to OG North? We do understand what explains it, but, nevertheless, the Chamber, as I said before, would like to have a look at the -- at these documents. Some examples I mentioned in the submissions of Croatia. May I take at that that they were provided to the Prosecution and are in the -- to some extent, unopened boxes? Is that correctly understood? I see everyone nodding yes on the Croatian side, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KESER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the documents you're referring to were sent, together with our reports. We have them here in digital form as well, and we can present them on our screens, if you wish to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't like to have a look at it now, right away, but rather have a look at it -- because the Chamber has to further consider all the arguments and -- but if there is a practical way of avoiding that we have to go through all of the series of documents -- again, I certainly did not look into the boxes. I mainly focused on the submissions by the parties and some matters that were specifically brought to our attention in this context. But if there's any practical way of identifying them so that it is easily -- easy to print them out, that would be appreciated. Perhaps by sending another copy to -- to the Chamber's staff. And we do understand that they have been submitted already. It's just a matter of finding them among the huge amount of documents that were received and which we did not want to look at in too much detail. The same would be true, then, for the reports by OG North command submitted to the HV Main Staff Operations Command Centre, that those would be included in that as well. Thank you. Anything else to be said about these documents? If not, we move to the next series. But we'll have little time because we also have to discuss further how to proceed. We'll certainly not finish this exercise today. The next one would be number 2 on the list, which is an order to attack Operational Group North to TRS-2. This document has been received; I understand that. The importance would rather be why this one is received and the others not. The explanation was given that it was the specific constellation that only HVO units were supported by TRS-2, which explains why this report exists. Now, one of the first things, we received a list of documents that were received in the 7th of December filing. Now, this report is mentioned in that list as an excerpt being received. Is that correctly understood, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I must confess I'm somewhat confused. We're talking about the order for attack OG North to TRS-2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 2 on the list is - and let me check again - is order for attack OG North to TRS-2, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding, and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, but this document is 65 ter 1639 and was in the possession of OTP before they filed their Rule 54 bis motion in June of 2008. I thought that was agreed. But maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, the point is not that the OTP has been pointing out that we have this document; the point is that we don't have the orders for TRS-1 and TS-3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I started with this one, because on the list of received documents -- and, of course, what we have on the 65 ter lists, I hope you will excuse us for not knowing all the details. But this report was also mentioned, I think, in the 7th of December filing as being received, but an excerpt being received. But we could check that. Let me get that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it bears the title: "Excerpt," on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, then, creates the next question: Where the full version is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's exactly right. It's the excerpt relevant to TRS-2, which further raises the question I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You say if this is an excerpt and covers the whole of TRS-2, where is TRS-1 and where is TRS-3? Because those are the numbers 1 and 3 on the list. The explanation that it was only HVO units that were supported by TRS-2, and in addition to that, an explanation of why a document is called an excerpt, and where is then the rest of it. First question to you, Mr. Tieger: Any further submissions in relation that -- to the fact that only HVO units were supported as the explanation given why this one is available and the others not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think, in previous discussions -- well, in any event, I think just one further point would be that I believe that TRS-1 also provided support to the HVO. But apart from that issue, I think we've made the other points in our previous submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not to say that you did not, but this hearing is aiming at finding out where we are with this -- you say there is nothing specifically to be added to that. Could I ask the representatives of the Republic of Croatia, excerpt, apart from the HVO and apart from the comments already made by Mr. Tieger, what explains the word "excerpt"? Which clearly suggests that there's more. Mr. Keser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KESER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I answer your question, allow me to make one point which I believe is very important. This order, which has been taken as an illustration as having been delivered is not an order for the TRS-group 2; it is an order for the infantry units of the HVO which were given certain tasks before the commencement of Operation Storm. This order was made before the main order issued by General Gotovina for Operation Storm. You can see from the order that the start of attack was scheduled for the 3rd of August. Now, the main order by General Gotovina schedules the start of Operation Storm for the 4th of August. In other words, it was only after the main order by General Gotovina and the ensuing documents set out the disposition of TS and TRS for Operation Storm. This particular order relates to an earlier structure for an action that followed operation Summer 95, so it was an action that took place between Summer 95 and Operation Storm. That's why we believe that the fact that it says excerpt for TRS-2 that there should be one for 3 or 1, because this is an order that was issued at the time that I stated. Furthermore, the document that was sent by the Croatian government was sent as an additional possible source of information and not as a -- as a document sought under item 2. The title of that document is: Order for attack for OG North for TRS-2. It is our position that in -- important information from the document as it is sought is the order of commander of Split Military District of the 1st of August, 1995. The existence of this document does not indicate that there were orders for TRS-1 and TRS-3 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is there, then, misunderstanding between the Office of the Prosecutor and the Republic of Croatia on whether or not the document they were seeking was received or not? Because you say we send it but not as one of the documents sought, but as a document which sheds some light on whether or not the document sought does exist. Is there mal-communication, or is there no mal-communication? Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, I was not aware of the position that this was -- this document has not yet been provided. And in -- so it appears there is some level of miscommunication, as reflected in the comments today. I suppose I could go back over the previous submissions by both sides to see if that is reflected in -- in -- if my understanding is reflected in the earlier submissions or if the position taken today is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's a matter to be sorted out between the Republic of Croatia and -- because the document is now reported as being received. I have not received an answer yet on my question why this is an excerpt and where the remainder of that document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise are we still talking about the order for attack of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about a document -- I mean, the identity of the document may be unclear, because apparently the Prosecution thinks that they have received a document they asked for, whereas, the Croatian Government says the document we provided is not the document you asked for. So, therefore, don't blame me at this moment for this type of confusion. It is the document which is in the initial list described as - let there be no doubt about that - as order for attack OG North to TRS-2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, first I have to correct the record, because we have -- in e-court the exhibit number is 65 ter 2606, which is a complete document, as -- as far as can I tell in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the title of the document does not start with excerpt?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, it does not. It's OG North commanders order for -- Oh, I'm sorry, I see excerpt on that, on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore -- Mr. Misetic intervened. Could you explain to me where the full document is. The document apparently is relevant. You provided it in this context. Could you provide the full document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KESER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, although we cannot deny that the title of the document states "excerpt," we have not been able to find a single fact that would point to the existence of a document of which this would be only a part. Because what is contained here only tasks for the HVO units which were supposed to carry out simulation of an attack, to a simulated attack before Operation Storm. The other units involved in Operation Storm received complete information in the orders that followed subsequently. So there would not exist a document which would have been made prior to this one and of which this would only be a part. We believe this document to be a full document, since the searches of the archive did not point to an existence of a document which could be connected to this. This document contains tasks issued to manoeuvre units. That's why we don't believe it is relevant, nor did we submit it as a replacement for this category of documents. In our position, this particular category of documents should not have been made to begin with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But they were made for one reason or another and they were, in the title, apparently, as it has been provided, it says "excerpt." Now, if you say, Well, we didn't find anything else, that, therefore, we believe it was a complete report. Let's be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We're coming to the -- to the dilemma. I'm looking at the document in e-court. In the upper right-hand corner, it is noted attachment 11. My staff tells me that because it is an excerpt, because it is an attachment to General Gotovina's wider order, the Kozjak attack order, and this is an attachment order to the wider order of General Gotovina, so this is an excerpt of General Gotovina's wider order, and we're in the process of looking for the admitted exhibit number of the Kozjak attack order, because I'm sure that is in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that apparently is a matter further to be explored and to see whether there is any confusion yes or no. It is close to a quarter to 2.00. We have to finish. I asked the parties to think about out-of-court sessions. I'm not saying that no Judge would be involved in it, but perhaps not the full court. You may have noticed that to some extent it is an administrative exercise, to some extent. We are not hearing evidence at this moment. At least that's not what we are seeking to do. Could I hear, first of all, from Croatia, whether a Croatian delegation would be willing to participate in such preparatory meetings in order to save time in court. And when looking at the accused, I can be -- it could be that they are not really excited by the type of information that went over the tables today. A lot of people are involved in these kind of court sessions, whereas a small number of people, most likely, if procedurally acceptable, could prepare for those meetings. What would be the position of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARKOTIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since we have expressed our openness and readiness to meet with representatives and specialists of the OTP, and since we have, in relation to these 158 categories carried out thorough searches, we express our readiness to resume our discussions with representatives of the OTP and Defence whenever practicable and as soon as possible, because it is under these circumstances -- or, rather, it is precisely these circumstances that are most to the detriment to Croatia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in those meetings, as suggested, Chamber's staff and perhaps even one of the Judges would participate. Would that change anything, Mr. Markotic, because the context you were referring to was without Judges? But I see you nodding that that would not make any difference. It would be a kind of meeting preparing the matters as we did today, in court, to see what remains to be discussed, really, as contested in court. Mr. Tieger, position of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, of course, we're prepared at any time to advance this process. I believe that, at this stage of the process meaningful progress will only be achieved with the presence of one or more of the Judges, and I think it is probably advisable also to keep some kind of record of the proceedings so that no ambiguity or confusion or other problems arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree with you that the practicalities and the transparency of such proceedings should be guaranteed and, of course, that proper attention should be paid to that before we exchange in any such discussions out of the courtroom. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, not only are we for that option, we strongly encourage the Chamber to schedule such a -- I don't want to be -- maybe the word mediation which you used last week with respect to a different issue. But I think it is quite clear - this issue has been pending for almost 20 months - that absent the Trial Chamber's direct involvement in this issue and guidance, it is destined to be unresolved, and I think all parties here have expressed a strong desire to get this issue resolved. So we would encourage the Chamber. We will, of course, participate any time, any place, to get to the bottom of it and resolve it. So we would encourage the Chamber to schedule this and to participate in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It seems more appropriate that this exercise we've going through today should be dealt with perhaps in a more informal way as it is administrative, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, to some extent, administrative, and, of course, any matter in dispute which remains. It's, of course, also judicial to the extent that we're talking about a motion and we are talking about orders, and we're talking about whether the Republic of Croatia has satisfied its obligations and has met its own targets and goals in this respect. So although the administrative level of it was quite high, it is like housekeeping sessions when we are admitting documents into evidence. We call that housekeeping, but, of course, it is part of judicial process. Not to say that you denied that, but I just want to emphasise that when I use the word "administrative," it is not to say that this Chamber is not in a position where it has to decide on matters that were put before them in their judicial quality. I take it that that's -- but I do see that you support. I just want to avoid any misunderstanding about what is administration and what is adjudication. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on part of Markac Defence we are much in favour of the suggestion because I think we share the mutual impression that there is an burden of ambiguity of the cooperation of the Republic of Croatia, even in this process. So I think that such meetings could resolve the problem in much more efficient way than it could be done elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. The Chamber will further consider this option. It is unlikely that we would have resolved this matter before the recess, which begins this Friday at 5.00. We'll be in touch with the parties. We have carefully listened to the observations made by the Croatian government, by the Prosecution, and by the Defence. Before we adjourn today, I -- first of all, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, although some of you have not yet had an opportunity to contribute to what was discussed today, I take it that in the background you all already have made your contribution. Therefore, Mr. Markotic, Mr. Crncec, Mr. Keser, Mr. Sklepic, Ms. Pokupec, Mr. Cule - already for the second time, short notice - and Mr. Bijelic, I would like to thank you all very much for coming to The Hague. You will be informed about any further steps to be taken by this Chamber. Unless there is anything which needs urgent attention at this moment, I would like to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is one issue that we had vis-a-vis Croatia that is left over from Friday's session. I don't know if can I raise that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm hesitant --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the Republic of Croatia indicated at the end of Friday's session that they would be producing correspondence which we haven't received from the Republic of Croatia yet. There was a second issue with respect to notes of meetings between the Prosecutor and Croatian officials that you had identified Ambassador Paro to check with his government on. I've had a discussion during the break with Mr. Markotic. With respect to those notes, there's an issue concerning whether there is commentary in there that they wouldn't disclosed. I'm perfect prepared to accept redacted notes that would redact any commentary, just so we can get to the bottom of what was discussed. So if we could perhaps resolve when, A, we would get the first portion which was stated that we would get; and, B, whether we can get the second portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cule was present last Friday. Mr. Markotic you seem to be head of the delegation today. I leave it to you who responds to the two questions put by Mr. Misetic. First, the correspondence, when to be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARKOTIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as we return, that's to say, tomorrow, we will hand over the correspondence. If my understanding is correct, that's correspondence between Prosecutor Brammertz and the justice minister. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, unless there was any other communication between the Prosecutor and someone else on the Croatian side, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the next -- yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Expressly including Prosecutor Bajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, specifically Mr. Misetic was speaking the communication between Croatian authorities and the Office of the Prosecution and specifically also including Mr. Bajic. We will then hear from you, I take it. Second question, the notes. Mr. Misetic suggests that you redact the comments in it. Has the Republic of Croatia already taken a position in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARKOTIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, up until we were about to leave Zagreb yesterday, we weren't really aware of what it is exactly that we were being sought to provide. When we return tomorrow, we will examine the request and send what has been sought. We have done so in the past as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would need the transcript of the hearing to review exactly what Mr. Misetic was seeking, then please ask for it, and it will be provided. If there's no other matter, I would like to, first of all, to thank you interpreters and transcribers and security, all those who stayed, and I am aware that my reputation gets worse and worse for another 12 minutes. We have no hearing tomorrow, I do understand, Mr. Mikulicic, that your next witness would be ready on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, we adjourn until Friday, the 18th of December, at 9.00 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of December, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.57 p.m.,
